{{Nihongo|{{ill|Ikagashiko-o|ja|伊香色雄|en:draft|Ikagashiko-o}}|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} was a Japanese mythological figure.<ref name="Chamberlain-Basil-1882a" /> His sister was {{ill|Ikagashikome|en|Ikagashikome}}.

== Mythical narrative ==
During Emperor Sujin's reign, a major epidemic and political crisis<ref name="aston150–164">{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_oEfAAAAYAAJ|title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Volume 2|author=Aston, William George.|date=1896|publisher=The Japan Society London|isbn=9780524053478|pages=150–164|author-link=William George Aston|qq=draft}}</ref> This led tim ho make major religious reforms to resolve it.<ref name="aston150–164" /> <ref name="aston150–164" /><ref name="Ellwood-1990a">{{Cite journal|last=Ellwood|first=Robert S.|date=1990|title=The Sujin Religious Revolution|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30234018|journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies|volume=17|issue=2/3|pages=199–217|doi=10.18874/jjrs.17.2-3.1990.199-217|issn=0304-1042|jstor=30234018}}</ref> .<ref name="aston150–164" />

Out of an abundance of caution, the Emperor also appointed {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ikagashikoo|ja|伊香色雄|en:draft|Ikagashikoo}}|伊香色雄|1=Ikagashiko-o}} as {{Nihongo|''kami-no-mono-akatsu-hito''|神班物者}}, or one who sorts the offerings to the gods.<ref name="Chamberlain-Basil-1882a">{{cite book |author=Chamberlain, Basil |url=http://www.sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj072.htm |title=''[SECT. LXV.—EMPEROR SŪ-JIN (PART III: STORY OF OHO-TATA-NE-KO'S BIRTH)]'' (''The Kojiki'') |publisher=Read before the Asiatic Society of Japan on April 12, May 10, and June 21, 1882, reprinted in 1919 |page=219 |quote=His Augustness Oho-tata-ne-ko&nbsp;... was the ancestor of the Dukes of Miwa and of the Dukes of Kamo. |author-link=Basil Chamberlain}}</ref>  {{ill|Ikagashikoo|ja|伊香色雄|en:draft|Ikagashikoo}} became the ancestor of the now extinct {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|Mononobe clan}}.<ref name="Chamberlain-Basil-1882a" />

He first enshrined {{ill|Futsu-no-mitama|fr|en:draft}} at Isonokami Shrine.<ref> https://nippon-kichi.jp/article_list.do?ml_lang=en&p=1390</ref>

Afterwards, the Emperor ordered Ikashikio to make the many hiraka pots, like those of the Mononobe clan, into offerings to the deities (kamimatsurimono, or offerings at divine festivals), and to make Otataneko the chief priest of Omononushi-no-Okami and Ichiisonagaoichi the chief priest of Yamato-Okunitama-no-Kami. As a result, the epidemic subsided, the country became peaceful, the grains grew, and the peasants prospered. <ref>『日本書紀』崇神天皇7th year pp月13日条</ref>

This is the only scene in which Ikashikio appears, but from it we can see that Emperor Sujin implemented a policy of unity of religion and politics by worshiping the god of {{ill|Mount Miwa|en|Mount Miwa|qid=Q860627|lt=Mount Miwa}} {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|qid=Q907495|lt=in Yamato Province}}, thereby solidifying the foundation of the Yamato government and beginning to unify the surrounding countries. <ref>中央公論社『日本の歴史1』p281 - 282</ref>

'''Ikagashiko no Mikoto''' (伊香色雄命) was a [[Kofun period]] nobleman and the progenitor of the [[Mononobe clan|Mononobe lineage]] according to records like the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} and {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}. He was appointed "Kami Mono Akatsuhito" (神班物者) to officiate over the worship of {{ill|Ōmononushi|en|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi}} in the 7th year of Emperor Sujin's reign. He is described as a sixth-generation descendant of {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}.<ref name="tenson">{{Sfn|Izumi City History Editorial Committee|1965|p=84}}</ref>

== Records ==
According to the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}, during Emperor Sujin's reign, a plague caused widespread mortality. In a divine revelation, the deity Ōmononushi appeared in the Emperor's dream, instructing him to appoint Ōtataneko as his priest, promising peace in the land. The Emperor followed this divine command:
{{quotation|Ōtataneko was thus appointed as the head priest, worshipping Ōmononushi at Mount Miwa. Additionally, Ikagashiko no Mikoto was commanded to prepare offerings for the gods, thus restoring peace and ending the plague.<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=Kojiki: Middle Volume|publisher=小学館|date=1983}}</ref>}}

The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} presents a similar account, adding that Emperor Sujin's daughters were instructed to serve {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}} and {{ill|Yamato Okunitama|en|Yamato Okunitama|qid=Q11387080|lt=Yamato no Ōkunitama}}.<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=Nihon Shoki, Volume V|publisher=岩波文庫|date=1994}}</ref> Ikagashiko no Mikoto was subsequently entrusted with overseeing rituals related to these deities, solidifying his role as a pivotal figure in the early Yamato polity.<ref>{{Cite book|和書|author=宇治谷孟|title=全現代語訳 日本書紀 上|publisher=講談社学術文庫|date=1988}}</ref>

== Stone Chambers and the Sacred Sword ==
Ikagashiko is credited with initiating the worship of the sacred sword {{ill|Futsu-no-mitama|ja|韴霊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futsu no Mitama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 布都御魂|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11059754}} at {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|en|Isonokami Shrine|qid=Q708859|lt=Isonokami Shrine}}, following Emperor Sujin’s directive.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.isonokami.jp/about/c2.html |title=Official Site of Isonokami Shrine |access-date=2024-04-29 }}</ref>

== Genealogy ==
The father of this lineage is identified as {{ill|Ōhesoki|ja|大綜麻杵命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsomahiki-no-Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q106106718}}, and the mother is Takaya-Awarahime (高屋阿波良姫). He is said to have had four wives: Maki-hime (真木姫), Ara-hime (荒姫), and Tamate-hime (玉手姫), daughters of the ancestor of the {{ill|Yamashiro no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|山代県主|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamashiro Agatanushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 山背国造|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11470858}}, Nagamizo; and Matori-hime (真鳥姫), daughter of {{ill|Yamato-shiki no Hikome|ja|倭志紀彦}}. Through these unions, he fathered numerous progeny, who became ancestors of various clans and lineages.

* '''With Maki-hime (真木姫):'''
** '''Takenokokoro Ōnemi no Mikoto (建胆心大禰命):''' Ancestor of the {{ill|Mononobe no Muraji|ja|物部連公}} lineage.
** '''Tabeno Sukune no Mikoto (多辨宿禰命):''' Ancestor of {{ill|Ujibe no Muraji|ja|宇治部連}}, {{ill|Hata no Imiki|ja|秦忌寸}}, {{ill|Katsuno|ja|葛野野}}, {{ill|Kurisu no Muraji|ja|栗栖連}}, {{ill|Ujiyamamoribe no Muraji|ja|宇治山守連}}, and {{ill|Haseyama no Ason|ja|長谷山直}}.

* '''With Ara-hime (荒姫):'''
** '''Amake Takemi no Mikoto (安毛建美命):''' Ancestor of the Mononobe no Muraji, {{ill|Rokujinabe no Muraji|ja|六人部連}}, {{ill|Minatori no Miyatsuko|ja|水取造}}, {{ill|Minatori no Muraji|ja|水取連}}, and {{ill|Tsukikome no Sukune|ja|舂米宿禰}}.
** '''Ōnikawa no Mikoto (大新河命):''' Ancestor of {{ill|Haseokihajime no Muraji|ja|長谷置始連}}, {{ill|Takahashi no Muraji|ja|高橋連}}, {{ill|Yatabe no Miyatsuko|ja|矢田部造}}, {{ill|Yatsudomi no Muraji|ja|矢集連}}, {{ill|Sayabe no Ason|ja|佐夜部直}}, {{ill|Sayabe no Obito|ja|佐夜部首}}, {{ill|Kuno no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|久努国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kunu no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q85875681}}, {{ill|hasetsukabeuji|ja|丈部氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takebe|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55530004}}, {{ill|ochinokuninomiyatsuko|ja|小市国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koichi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q21652684}} (ancestor of the {{ill|Ochi clan|ja|越智氏|Ochi clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ochi no Obito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11636555}}), {{ill|kazahayanokuninomiyatsuko|ja|風速国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazehaya no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q21652739}} (ancestor of the Kazehaya no Obito), and {{ill|Karube no Miyatsuko|ja|軽部造}}.

* '''With Tamate-hime (玉手姫):'''
** '''Tochinone no Mikoto (十市根命):''' Ancestor of {{ill|Mononobe no Tokone|ja|物部十千根|qid=Q24885356}}.
** '''Takenokawa no Mikoto (建新川命):''' Ancestor of the {{ill|Yamato-shiki Agatanushi|ja|倭志紀県主}}, {{ill|Ōyake no Obito|ja|大宅首}}, {{ill|Kawakami no Miyatsuko|ja|川上造}}, and {{ill|Harumichi no Sukune|ja|春道宿禰}}.

* '''With Matori-hime (真鳥姫):'''
** '''Ōburafu no Mikoto (大売布命):''' Ancestor of the Yamato-shiki Agatanushi (志紀連), {{ill|Tōichibe no Obito|ja|十市部首}}, {{ill|Kuji Kokuzō|ja|久自国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuji no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11369664}}, {{ill|Ōbe no Miyatsuko|ja|大部造}}, {{ill|Magakibe no Miyatsuko|ja|真髪部造}}, {{ill|Wakayusumaro no Muraji|ja|若湯坐連}}, {{ill|Arimichi no Sukune|ja|有道宿禰}}, {{ill|Imaki no Muraji|ja|今木連}}, and {{ill|Izumi Shiki Agatanushi|ja|和泉志紀県主}}.

Additionally, genealogical traditions from sources such as the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}} include {{ill|Makandakone no Muraji|ja|真神田曽禰連}}, {{ill|Makanda no Obito|ja|真神田首}}, and {{ill|Sone no Muraji|ja|曽根連}}, tracing their lineage to a son named {{ill|Kizubetsu no Mikoto|ja|気津別命}}.

== Worship ==
Ikagashiko is enshrined at {{ill|Ikagashi Shrine|ja|伊加加志神社|qid=Q11378911}}, an ancient shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}. It is located in {{ill|Yoshinogawa, Tokushima|en|Yoshinogawa, Tokushima|qid=Q592500|lt=Yoshinogawa}}, Tokushima Prefecture.
